patients.label: 13-year-old girl with motor and vocal tics later diagnosed with atypical PKAN

identity_evidence.quote: A 13-year-old girl was evaluated at the psychiatric service for motor and vocal tics.

attribution_limitations: The article says the symptoms resembled typical Tourette syndrome ("apparent typical symptoms of TS") and the title says they did not match it; no Tourette syndrome diagnosis is stated as made or refuted for this patient, so no Tourette syndrome condition is recorded.
The author hypothesis that basal ganglia dysfunction from iron accumulation promoted the Tourette-like symptoms is a hedged mechanism, not an established cause, and is not recorded as a fact.

The source does not say which treatment (pimozide, risperidone or topiramate) the "poor response to treatment" refers to, so the poor-response event is not ordered against the risperidone/topiramate switch; the order of the MRI and the genetic testing relative to each other is also not stated.

Dates are relative only (two years earlier, one year after the first evaluation, ten months after the diagnosis); no calendar dates and no absolute ages for later events.

Pimozide dose, duration and the dates of the MRI and genetic testing are not stated; no allergy, family history, social, oncology or care-plan documentation is present.
